scope: P9 bounded private P2P/group screen video selected resolution/FPS and live source quality
behavior: P2P screen capture uses selected device preferences, resolves native Windows physical metrics after the user picker, and applies resolution/FPS plus encoding bitrate ceilings. Pending sources remain disabled until exact active-call/auth/PC/localStream and sender ownership checks pass.

Group screen capture uses the existing actual admitted SDK Room; SDKConnected, canPublish, current capture admission, account generation and current group key epoch are required. Captured SDK screen tracks are muted through publication and unmuted only after current lease checks.

Quality/FPS changes apply constraints and sender encoding ceilings to the existing owned source; no picker reopen or new Room. Group primary and backup codec senders retain source identity. Codec changes are not attempted as a live quality update.

Late permission/picker/SDK publication results cannot publish into a replacement call or Room. Reconnect/admission closure, auth generation, group epoch or component retirement stops the owned source. A reconnect requires explicitly sharing again; selected device preferences remain saved.

P2P pending camera changes prevent screen acquisition with explicit retry guidance; the companion camera slice treats a pending/active screen ticket as local-preview-only, preventing competing same-sender replacements. Stopping screen sharing restores the latest local camera track.

P2P renegotiation wait is bounded to 10 seconds, closed/retired peers release capture, and a negotiated video transceiver with a cleared sender is reused. Initial capture/quality failure restores the still-current camera sender and stops the screen source.

Private calls are explicitly video-only in this bounded slice. Native system audio remains owned by the existing guild capture helper; no private WASAPI ownership or capture lease was added. Existing guild selected-quality runtime is preserved.

Review correction: every P2P camera/screen replaceTrack and screen setParameters mutation shares one actual-sender queue. Stop retains a restore ticket through awaited replacement, restores the latest local camera after deferred preview updates, removes screen-only FPS/bitrate caps and prevents stale queued mutations from overwriting a newer owner. A new picker waits for restoration; auth/call cleanup invalidates old restore continuations.
